root_cause_summary.interpretation: The six misses are heterogeneous: direct retrieval failures, article-selection/body-event failures caused by headline-level triage, and one evidence-composition failure. Hardening therefore adds targeted layers rather than globally weakening locality or temporal thresholds.

trusted_source_domain_universe.derivation: Domains already represented in accepted Slice 1 historical/research evidence and independent Slice 1 hits; domain membership only widens retrieval and never confers a positive classification.

discovery_rules_changed.rule: If generic per-episode web/news and Telegram searches yield no qualifying hit, generate fallback queries from the target episode's exact local date, Zaporizhzhia locality terms, explosion/strike vocabulary, aerial-war vocabulary, and the episode's local-hour envelope across the existing trusted/relevant domain universe. The fallback may surface a URL but never auto-accepts it.
discovery_rules_changed.generalizable_because: It responds to repeated indexable-source retrieval failures and is parameterized only by episode fields plus a source-domain universe, not by control IDs, dates, URLs, or historical verdicts.

discovery_rules_changed.rule: For every retained article, inspect the full available body and split it into separate event statements/passages. For each event independently record locality, explosion/impact/PVO-only type, aerial-war context, event time or temporal wording, and relation to the target alert.
discovery_rules_changed.generalizable_because: Multi-event news articles routinely combine locations and updates; event-level extraction prevents lead/headline bias without lowering evidence thresholds.

discovery_rules_changed.rule: Headline labels are retrieval metadata only. A PVO-forward headline or a headline about another locality cannot classify the whole article if the body contains a separate event statement. PVO_ONLY remains non-positive when no body event supplies independent explosion/impact evidence.
discovery_rules_changed.generalizable_because: It separates article framing from event evidence while preserving the existing PVO-only precision guard.

discovery_rules_changed.rule: Locality is assigned per extracted event statement. Explosion evidence from one locality may never be transferred to a Zaporizhzhia statement merely because both appear in one article.
discovery_rules_changed.generalizable_because: It addresses multi-locality articles and explicitly blocks the main false-positive risk introduced by full-body extraction.

discovery_rules_changed.rule: Complementary source or passage components may be composed only when they describe the same attack/event sequence, have compatible locality and timing, and add non-conflicting evidence. Preserve provenance for every component. Composition alone cannot promote ambiguous evidence to strict unless an independent strict basis exists.
discovery_rules_changed.generalizable_because: It reconstructs legitimate same-attack chains while preventing arbitrary assembly of unrelated region, city, and time facts.

unchanged_temporal_guardrails: publication time is not event time
publication/update lag cannot create a positive for a later episode
neighboring Telegram messages may clarify chronology only when they form one compatible attack chain
wrong-episode candidates are rejected or rematched to the episode supported by event chronology
cumulative updates do not create a new event automatically

implementation_scope.reason: The Slice 0B and Slice 1 discovery workflow on this branch is encoded as research methodology/artifacts rather than a reusable executable historical-discovery module. Hardening is therefore recorded as reproducible discovery rules and rerun provenance; no live-monitor code is touched.
